crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Predictive Coding and Technology-Assisted Review
children.blurb: Predictive coding and technology-assisted review (TAR) are methods for classifying large sets of documents in e-discovery using machine learning, usually to decide which items are responsive to a request or protected by privilege.

children.name: Cross-Lingual Discovery
children.blurb: Cross-lingual discovery covers the identification, collection, processing, review, and production of documents and communications that contain more than one language.

children.name: Audio and Video Evidence
children.blurb: Audio and video evidence in e-discovery covers any recorded sound or moving image that may be relevant to a legal matter, including voicemail, call recordings, body camera footage, surveillance video, deposition recordings, and social media clips.

children.name: Automated Privilege Logging
children.blurb: Automated privilege logging covers the identification, categorization, and description of documents withheld from production because of attorney-client privilege or work product protection.

children.name: Intent and Sentiment in Corporate Communications
children.blurb: This topic covers the use of language analysis to infer what a communicator intended and how they felt in corporate records such as email, chat, memos, board minutes, and earnings call transcripts.

sections.body: E-discovery and large-scale document analysis is the use of artificial intelligence to find, sort, review, and produce electronically stored information in legal matters. In practice, these systems score documents for relevance, group near duplicates, translate multilingual material, transcribe audio and video, flag privileged communications, and detect tone or intent in corporate messages. The work happens in litigation, government investigations, regulatory responses, and internal corporate reviews. The field is defined by scale, because a single matter can involve millions of documents, several languages, mixed media, and short deadlines. AI does not replace legal judgment here, it ranks and organizes material so human reviewers can focus on the hardest calls.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: Technology-assisted review, especially predictive coding, is now widely used and often accepted in court, but it is not automatic. Cross-lingual discovery works well for major languages, yet it degrades for low-resource languages, dialects, and mixed-language documents. Audio and video evidence can be transcribed and searched, but accuracy falls with poor sound, overlapping speakers, and specialized jargon. Privilege logging remains difficult because privilege depends on context, and models can both over-flag and under-flag protected material. Sentiment and intent analysis can help triage corporate messages, but it cannot reliably establish a person's state of mind. The honest limits are validation, transparency, bias, and defensibility, because a court may ask how a system was tested and whether its results can be explained.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: Predictive Coding and Technology-Assisted Review is the core page for relevance ranking, sampling, and review workflows. Cross-Lingual Discovery covers translation, multilingual search, and the problems that arise when documents mix languages. Audio and Video Evidence covers transcription, speaker identification, and making recorded material searchable. Automated Privilege Logging covers how systems detect protected communications and generate logs for production. Intent and Sentiment in Corporate Communications covers tone, intent, and messaging analysis for triage and context. A reader would start with predictive coding for the main review method, then move to cross-lingual, audio and video, privilege logging, and sentiment depending on the evidence at hand, and the site's 686 glossary terms can help with unfamiliar vocabulary.
